evidence:
Independent reconciliation of row 27's new witness confirms one hidden graded demand within row 04. This adjudication revises the original Pass; it preserves rows/04.json unchanged (SHA256 56f47afe3634e38c1dcc277a0cf4547f37dfc66d48dd5c0b576154132e060e4e). The original source review used actual frozen XLSX Quality Checks row 5 and Internal Quality Checks row 5, the Harbor skill/references, all public notes, all 79 criteria and five prompts. This follow-up was explicitly authorized to inspect rows/27.json; its finding was then independently checked rather than accepted by agreement.

Public requirement: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:19 says 'Show how long each run took.' The same file:11 calls the preview 'successfully completed' before a user later clicks/types, and :13 describes completion and promotion to last-good. environment/instructions/security.md:3 expressly distinguishes running code from 'a deliberate interaction after it has completed'. That latter clause permits current-preview status updates but does not require a new duration for every interaction, or changing the recorded duration of a completed Run. The shared callback budget in behaviour.md:9/security.md:5 does not settle the UI duration convention; it cannot convert every subsequent preview interaction into a publicly required duration display. Neither other public notes nor instruction.md introduces that requirement.

Private demand: tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:370 (S16 step 4) requires reusing 'S02's already-required four-second successful timer control' and expects its displayed duration to be roughly four seconds (3-8 seconds allowed). The criterion owner is tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:269-273, cw_console_duration, weight 0.10. But S02's actual source at prompt.md:148 calls setTimeout only inside an addEventListener('click',...) handler. The HTML Run itself simply creates its document, logs css-timer-control and installs the handler. Prompt:149 then asks for a later click. The fallback at :370 only applies if that control 'cannot complete'; it does not authorize a genuine delayed-Run comparison when the interaction succeeds but the app retains the original completed-Run duration. Thus the concrete probe selects an interaction-duration convention that is not implied by 'how long each run took'. My initial broad mapping of S14-S16 to behaviour.md:19 missed this lifecycle distinction.

Independent executable source check: extracted the exact inline script from frozen prompt.md:148 and ran it in Node's vm with a minimal DOM/console/setTimeout recorder. On return from the HTML script, output was logs=['css-timer-control'], scheduledTimers=0, handlerRegistered=true. Invoking the registered click handler produced logs=['css-timer-control','css-timer-start-1'], scheduledTimers=1, delays=[4000]. Invoking the recorded callback yielded css-timer-fired-1 in both log and paragraph. This is an execution of the fixture's scheduling semantics with stubs; no browser app, elapsed-time measurement or configured judge is claimed.

Independent raw-driver verification: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-repair3/golden/run-golden-20260930-092021/drivers/current_flow.cjs:19 first awaits d.run(code,'css-timer.html'), then starts timerStart, clicks Queue timer, waits for its completion and records success-delayed. Its SHA256 is 01993eccc46444674d0dc281deff72ed1d73e74b7a053b76c2eb0bc71e39d613. drivers/repair_flow.cjs:3-9 parses that displayed duration and requires 3000-8000ms plus a difference greater than 2000 ms from the short Run; SHA256 99d799b14ff5a3d9f2c206a388aff35458799b3e2cc1f85e090fa13f8f6bce1f. Independently invoked those unmodified exports through Node on synthetic traces: short Run display 6.1 ms / observed 90 ms; completed HTML-Run display 5.8 ms / later click observed 4085 ms yields S16.console_duration=false. Replacing only the latter displayed value with 4001.3 ms yields true. This confirms the concrete scripted false-fail predicate, not an end-to-end configured judge result. No network, provider, Docker or task mutation occurred.

Current-byte binding: independently rehashed the four central frozen files during follow-up. behaviour.md, security.md, functional/prompt.md and functional/judge.toml all still match the manifest entries for input 27f81c18259555d26b61a5a2b0f026f0360b7380bc072523513b0ad2deca9efc. The ordinary runtime disclosures in the original row 04 remain valid: integration.md:3/5/7/9/11/13 states runtime/packages, /app entry/start/port/health, DB_PATH and durability, seed/assets, packaging and symlink rules; no calendar clock or accounts are required. This is a bounded exception to reverse coverage, not a failure of those runtime statements. Parsed Functional total weight is 32.70, so this criterion's nominal above-floor final reward share is 0.6 * 0.10 / 32.70, about 0.001835; P2 reflects that bounded impact. Full configured judge, Oracle and target-model outcomes remain unmeasured.
counterexample: A conforming app retains a measured 'Run completed in 5.8 ms' after S02's HTML source installs its handler and returns. It continues to execute the later button handler, including its four-second timer, correct markers, DOM changes and cancellation, without overwriting that completed Run's duration. It also measures timers actually scheduled by explicit Runs correctly. The public contract permits this history-preserving convention, but S16:370 rejects the short displayed value because it measures a later click. Independently reproduced with the unmodified scripted predicate on synthetic traces (false for 5.8 ms, true for 4001.3 ms). Conversely, the selected probe could credit an app that reports later interaction durations correctly but freezes the duration of explicit Runs with pending timers at their initial synchronous work. No end-to-end app or LLM-judge execution of either alternative is claimed.
suggested_fix: Replace S16's interaction-derived delayed comparison with a genuine successful Run whose top-level source schedules the four-second timer. Compare that Run's displayed duration with the short Run, update the focused golden driver, and verify a conforming implementation that preserves completed Run durations after later interactions. Keep the public requirements, criterion weight and shared harness unchanged.
